rationale: The scraper landed on the locale home (/en-jp/) which typically doesn’t show product tiles and may display cookie/locale overlays. The safest fix is to avoid the homepage and directly enter a stable PLP (men/outerwear), while handling OneTrust consent. We add resilient selectors for Moncler's common product grid/card structures and generic PDP price/title fallbacks. URL rules normalize to the en-jp locale, redirect homepage to a canonical PLP, and deny non-moncler domains to avoid corporate/locale traps. Minimal overrides add Accept-Language, consent dismissal, and explicit wait targets to ensure the PLP materializes.
code_hints: After initial navigation, attempt to click consent: await clickIfVisible('#onetrust-accept-btn-handler', 2000).
If no PLP grid appears within 3s on /en-jp/, immediately navigate to /en-jp/men/outerwear/.
Guard against locale overlays; if a modal with a generic close button appears, dismiss via button[aria-label*='Close'] before scanning PLP.
Wait for PLP grid with: await page.waitForSelector("ul[data-testid='product-grid'], section [data-testid='product-grid'], section [class*='product-grid']", { timeout: 12000 });
Extract product links by querying within product_card for anchors starting with '/en-'; resolve to absolute with current origin.
On PDP, prefer [itemprop='price'] for robust price extraction; fallback to [data-testid*='pdp-price'] or .product-price.
Set extra HTTP headers: Accept-Language: en-JP,en;q=0.9; use a modern desktop UA string.
If PLP still empty, try nav clicks: await clickIfVisible("a[href*='/en-jp/men']", 2000); then await clickIfVisible("a[href*='/outerwear']", 2000).
Scroll PLP to load more (incremental scroll) and wait for network idle before extraction.
